co_mileski_wall.blurb: Mileski Wall is a band of steep cliff at God's Crag, high in the San Juan country outside Lake City. Ten routes are listed, nearly all of them bolted sport lines plus a single trad route, running from about 5.10 into the low 5.14s. Most sit in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, so this is a place for strong climbers rather than beginners. The stone is volcanic tuff, pocketed and steep, and routes run roughly 85 to 170 feet. A waterfall cuts through the wall, which can leave the base damp. To get to the wall you simply walk along the foot of the cliff band.

co_joyland_boulder.blurb: Joyland Boulder is a lone, easily recognised block on the Hillside Drive circuit in the Four Corners region, set in a cool aspen grove at roughly 9,400 feet. The sandstone offers pockets, crimps, slopers and rails across all four sides. Ten problems are listed, and half of them are V0 warm-ups, so it suits newer boulderers and groups mixing abilities. A few steeper lines step up to V3 and V5. The tops are low-angle enough to walk off, and the trail in is short and flagged, running past two neighbouring boulder clusters toward the west end of the bench.

co_coliseum_the.blurb: The Coliseum is a north-facing trad crag in the South Fork of St. Vrain Canyon, a few miles up the highway from Lyons. Because it sits in shade, it works well as a hot-weather choice. Ten routes are listed, with a little over half of them at 5.7 or 5.8 and a handful stretching to 5.10 and 5.11. Routes can reach about 200 feet, and many have bolted anchors. The base is reached over a talus field after crossing the creek, so expect some loose footing. It sees few visitors and feels quiet and remote, though lichen and loose rock are part of the deal.

co_moby_dick_boulder.blurb: Moby Dick Boulder is the largest block in the Mecca area of Unaweep Canyon, outside Grand Junction, and it sits within a short stroll of the namesake Mecca Boulder. Ten problems are listed, mostly V3 to V5, with a pair of harder lines up to about V6. The sandstone is good quality and the landings around the area are flat. Expect vertical, crimpy climbing. Like most of the Mecca zone it is exposed to the sun, which makes winter a pleasant time to visit and midsummer very hot. Gnats can be bothersome in late spring, and wet soil needs time to dry after storms.
